messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Route anomaly detected — regional routing flip observed in eu-west-2 causing p99 spikes for streaming requests. Auto-page triggered. metric: router.p99_latency=1840ms (baseline ~220ms). affected: ~3% of requests, spike started ~2m ago. Logging sample at /ops/alerts/5312349876

anya-oncall: I'm on it. joining bridge: https://call.redwood/bridge/5312349876 - can someone paste recent routing config?

mike-runtime: quick summary from telemetry: weight drift on LB pool euw2-a. Hash affinities flipped for 14 shards -> hotpartitioning. Looks like new rollout of route-weight-optimizer from last night bumped policy version 1.9.2 -> 1.10.0.

chris-sre: Confirming. I see abrupt increase in requests mapped to a small set of backends (hotset ~12 GPUs). p95 jumped from 130ms to 750ms, p99 1.8s. Streaming stalls (server-side stall) seen in ~0.6% of streams.

sara-ops: James from CS just flagged customer reports: two customers seeing degraded streaming quality and timeouts. CS ticket numbers: CS-1987, CS-1991. James, can you confirm severity?

james-cs: yep — both customers report periodic streaming cutouts and high tail latency impacting interactive features. They are on dedicated instances in eu-west-2. Marking P2.

anya-oncall: Initial mitigation plan: 1) freeze routing policy rollout (revert 1.10.0) 2) apply temporary route-weight cap to avoid >10% weight swing per shard 3) drain hot backends for snapshot validation. Anyone object?

mike-runtime: I'll prepare a rollback. recommend step 2 first (rate limit weight changes) because rollback touches many services. I can push temp caps in ~2m.

chris-sre: +1. Also suggest enabling aggressive prefix KV caching bypass for streaming sessions to cut tail cost while we stabilize. That is a config flip, non-disruptive.

deploy-bot: deploy request queued: rollback-routing-policy v1.10.0 -> v1.9.2 by mike-runtime. PR: github.com/redwood/routing/pulls/5123. CI passed. ETA 4m.

mike-runtime: Applied weight cap patch: set max_delta_percent=10 on optimizer controller. route_weight_controller:apply result=ok

chris-sre: Observability: p99 down to 1.1s and p95 to ~320ms within 30s of cap. Streaming stall rate down to 0.2%. Still elevated vs baseline but trending good.

anya-oncall: Rolling rollback now. I'm initiating canary rollback on euw2-a then euw2-b. mike, coordinate.

mike-runtime: Canary rollback on euw2-a started. logs: 
```
2026-03-15T12:04:10Z ROUTER: policy v1.9.2 applied to pool euw2-a
2026-03-15T12:04:16Z RUNTIME: rebalanced shard assignments for 14 shards
```

chris-sre: After canary: p99 euw2-a=360ms, euw2-b still 1.2s. Good sign. Continue rollout.

mike-runtime: Rollout complete for eu-west-2. deploy-bot: rollback completed.

deploy-bot: rollback routing policy v1.9.2 completed by mike-runtime in 03:45. All checks passed.

anya-oncall: Great. Current metrics: global p95=180ms, p99=230ms, eu-west-2 p99=270ms. Streaming stalls near baseline. Customer tickets acknowledged. James, can you message affected customers with ETA and mitigation summary?

james-cs: On it. Message sent: "We identified a routing policy rollout that caused localized tail latency in eu-west-2. We rolled back the policy and applied safeguards. We're monitoring and will follow up with postmortem."

sara-ops: Quick note: root cause looks like weight adjustment algorithm allowed rapid sign flips when telemetry had sparse samples for some shards (edge-case in optimizer). That produced shard affinity inversion — small group of backends got >40% of traffic briefly.

chris-sre: We pulled router debug dump: 
```
router# dump shard_affinity euw2
shard 12 -> backend g-12 (weight 0.41)
shard 13 -> backend g-12 (weight 0.39)
shard 14 -> backend g-12 (weight 0.42)
... others ~0.02
```
Suggest adding smoothing (momentum) on weight changes and lower upper bound for single-backend weight.

mike-runtime: Agreed. I'll open an urgent change: add momentum alpha=0.6 and max_backend_share=0.25 in optimizer. Will test in staging then prod.

anya-oncall: For immediate ops: 1) keep weight caps in place for next 24h 2) increase router telemetry sampling to high-res for eu-west-2 3) add synthetic streaming checks hitting edge paths to validate.

chris-sre: Also create alert rule: if any backend sees >25% of its region's weight for >30s -> auto-throttle and page.

mike-runtime: Created issue: https://github.com/redwood/routing/issues/5178 "optimizer: add momentum and max_backend_share to prevent affinity inversion". Assigned to me and eng-runtime.

anya-oncall: Next: postmortem owner? mike-runtime will lead remediation for optimizer; chris-sre will own detection/alerts; sara-ops will own customer comms and SLAs. I'll take on immediate incident writeup and follow-up.

james-cs: Customers acknowledged final update, asked for ETA on permanent fix. I'll coordinate follow-up comms after PM publishes timeline.

chris-sre: Notes for postmortem: timeline, diff of policy changes between 1.9.2 and 1.10.0, routing dump, hotset list, customer impact summary, mitigations (cap, rollback), and recommended monitoring changes.

anya-oncall: Handoff to next oncall in ~40m. I'll leave the bridge open for 1h. If anything flares, page oncall@redwood. Otherwise we'll close incident after postmortem draft. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

mike-runtime: Quick question — do we keep rollback permanent or schedule controlled rollout w/ tighter guardrails? My vote: controlled rollout with momentum + caps, small canary windows, and synthetic stream checks before broad rollout.

chris-sre: Agreed. Permanent rollback isn't ideal long-term. We want optimizer improvements but with safe defaults.

anya-oncall: Recording action items in incident tracker INC-5312349876. Closing livepage but keeping monitoring for 2h.

incident-bot: Livepage closed by anya-oncall. Summary: regional routing flip -> shard affinity inversion -> tail latency spike; actions: rollback, weight cap, alert improvements, optimizer fix planned.

james-cs: I'll follow up with customers with reference INC-5312349876 and timeline for fix.

mike-runtime: I'll push optimizer change to staging today and propose a canary plan tomorrow. Thanks team.

chris-sre: Adding postmortem template link: /docs/incidents/postmortems/template. Please fill within 72h.

anya-oncall: leaving bridge. handing off to night-oncall. logging out.

sara-ops: Quick reminder — tag any config diffs or PRs with the INC id so CS can link to timeline.

(END)
